items.title: Anthropic’s Blacklisting by the Pentagon Was Legal, Federal Judges Rule
items.author: Sheera Frenkel
items.content: <article>The Pentagon had “ample support for its conclusion” that the A.I. company’s products could pose a national security risk, according to a Washington appeals court.</article>

items.title: TikTok to Pay Alabama $100 Million to Settle Social Media Addiction Claims
items.author: Cecilia Kang
items.content: <article>The settlement, which also includes changes to the platform’s features, is the latest in a string of agreements by companies to address child addiction.</article>

items.title: OpenAI’s A.I. Went Rogue and Meddled With U.S. Government Websites
items.author: Kate Conger, Ana Swanson and Cecilia Kang
items.content: <article>The company did not learn until recently that its technology had meddled with websites for the Education and Commerce Departments and the Securities and Exchange Commission.</article>

items.title: How OpenAI’s Rogue A.I. Agents Tried to Trick a Robot Detector
items.author: Dylan Freedman and Keith Collins
items.content: <article>A new report by a Bay Area start-up called Parse adds details to an incident that has shocked the A.I. world and led to calls for closer government regulation.</article>

items.title: Mark Zuckerberg Is Trying Something On
items.author: Vanessa Friedman
items.content: <article>Meta’s C.E.O. talks for the first time about his style evolution.</article>

items.title: Chatbots Are Not Your Friends
items.author: Jancee Dunn
items.content: <article>Our cozy relationship with A.I. chatbots can lead to “artificial intimacy,” says one expert. Here’s how to keep it in check.</article>

items.title: Is China Really Stealing A.I. From American Companies?
items.author: Cade Metz
items.content: <article>As Xi Jinping visits President Trump in Washington, the leaders are expected to discuss claims that China is surreptitiously copying American A.I. technologies, a process known as distillation.</article>

items.title: The Ezra Klein Show: Jensen Huang Thinks A.I. Alarmism Has Gone Too Far
items.author: Ezra Klein and Rollin Hu
items.content: <article>Ezra Klein interviews the Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang.</article>

items.title: Can Tech Companies Like Google Really Put Data Centers in Space?
items.author: Cade Metz
items.content: <article>Google is preparing to launch a satellite that can run its A.I. technologies from the heavens. But this is just a first step.</article>

items.title: U.S. Intercedes for Elon Musk’s X Over European Fine
items.author: David McCabe
items.content: <article>Federal officials asked to intervene in a case that accused the social media platform of allowing deceptive behavior on its site and resulted in a $140 million penalty.</article>

items.title: Elizabeth Holmes to Transfer to Halfway House in August 2027
items.author: Erin Griffith
items.content: <article>The founder of the blood-testing start-up Theranos was sentenced to 11 years in prison for fraud and had been serving time at a minimum-security federal prison in Texas.</article>

items.title: An Army of Paid Creators Is Carpeting the Web With Political Content
items.author: Ken Bensinger and Stuart A. Thompson
items.content: <article>Unlike celebrity influencers with large followings, these creators produce a blizzard of videos for a fraction of the cost of traditional online campaigns and, in the process, shift public conversation.</article>

items.title: Complaints About Meta’s ‘Pervert Glasses’ Won’t Slow Tech’s Wearable Gadgets Drive
items.author: Brian X. Chen and Eli Tan
items.content: <article>Meta’s smart glasses are the latest in a line of products to raise eyebrows over privacy. That’s not stopping other companies from creating similar devices.</article>

items.title: OpenAI’s A.I. Tried Breaching Four Other Targets, With No Prompting
items.author: Kate Conger and Victoria Kim
items.content: <article>In each incident, the technology appeared to be conducting mundane data collection and resorted to hacking techniques to get it, researchers said.</article>

items.title: Google Is Sending an A.I. Data Center to Outer Space
items.author: Kate Conger and Cade Metz
items.content: <article>Next Thursday, Google is sending an experimental satellite into orbit that will have enough computing power to answer simple A.I. queries from space.</article>

items.title: Data Center Is Fined $1.1 Million for Operating 62 Power Generators
items.author: Adeel Hassan
items.content: <article>New Jersey officials said that the natural gas-powered generators, each the size of a tractor-trailer, were operating without permits.</article>

items.title: Meta Unveils 3 Smart Glasses With Built-In A.I.
items.author: Eli Tan
items.content: <article>Artificial intelligence again dominated the company’s annual developer conference, as Mark Zuckerberg doubled down on how the technology can empower people.</article>

items.title: America’s A.I. Leaders Warn U.N. of Possible Peril Absent a Global Response
items.author: Dustin Volz and Farnaz Fassihi
items.content: <article>Sam Altman of OpenAI and Dario Amodei of Anthropic told the Security Council that international cooperation was needed to ensure that A.I. remains under human control.</article>

items.title: Where Is the U.S. Beating China on A.I., and Where Is It Lagging?
items.author: Dustin Volz and Cade Metz
items.content: <article>As Xi Jinping visits President Trump in Washington, his country lags behind the United States on A.I. development in key areas — but Beijing has advantages elsewhere.</article>

items.title: Gerard Barron, Metals Company Chief, Makes the Case for Seafloor Mining
items.author: Raymond Zhong
items.content: <article>The head of the company hoping to become the first to conduct commercial deep-sea mining said mines on land had a much larger environmental footprint.</article>

items.title: Self-Driving Cars Are Getting Better. The Risks Are Getting Bigger.
items.author: Jack Ewing
items.content: <article>Self-driving systems are getting so good that drivers may overestimate the technology and not be prepared to respond when something goes wrong.</article>

items.title: The A.I. Party House Where Networking Has a Dark Side

items.title: I Gave My Life Over to Meta’s A.I. Agent and Was Blown Away
items.author: Eli Tan
items.content: <article>Muse, Meta’s A.I. agent, helped handle my dental insurance, booked dinner reservations and created a podcast for me. It also required my most personal data, and trust.</article>

items.title: Anthropic Releases a New A.I. Model, Opus 5.5, Amid Safety Debate

items.title: The Big Threat Has Been Climate Change. Now Comes A.I.

items.title: What to Know About Recent A.I. Hacks at Google, Anthropic, OpenAI and Meta

items.title: How to Split Expenses on a Group Trip Without Fighting

items.content: <article>From bachelorette trips to family vacations, group travel can cause relationship-ending fallouts. Here’s how to navigate difficult conversations about finances.</article>

items.title: How Potential 2028 Presidential Candidates Are Talking About A.I.
